source.title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)

accepted.question_text: For an integer n at least 3, characterize or represent the n-ary copulas C:[0,1]^n -> [0,1] that are associative in Post's sense: for all x1, ..., x_{2n-1} in [0,1], all ways of applying C to one consecutive block of n inputs and then applying C to the resulting n inputs give the same value. The goal is a structural representation for n-ary associative copulas analogous in purpose to the known classification of binary associative copulas.

For a fixed integer m at least 2, characterize the bivariate copulas C:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] that are m-ultramodular, meaning that for every k in {2,...,m} and all points (x,y),(u1,v1),...,(uk,vk) in [0,1]^2 for which every argument remains in [0,1]^2, the alternating finite-difference sum over all subsets J of {1,...,k} of (-1)^(k+|J|) C(x + sum_{i in J} ui, y + sum_{i in J} vi) is nonnegative. Also characterize the associative and Archimedean subfamilies of such copulas.

For a power-stable binary operation O:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1], where O(x^p,y^p)=O(x,y)^p for every p>0, determine how structural and regularity properties of O correspond to properties of the one-variable functions f and g that represent O in the standard power-stable forms O(x,y)=(xy)^{f(log(x)/log(xy))} and O(x,y)=(xy)^{g(log(x)/log(y))}. The properties to relate include monotonicity, continuity, the 1-Lipschitz property, associativity, and existence of a neutral element.

Fix x0 in the open unit interval. Characterize all functions delta:[0,1] -> [0,1] for which there exists a bivariate copula C such that C(x,x)=delta(x) for every x in [0,1] and C is linear on each segment connecting the diagonal point (x0,x0) to the corner points (1,0) and (0,1). Within this class, construct pointwise maximal and pointwise minimal copulas when they exist.

Let C_a be the class of associative bivariate copulas, equivalently the 1-Lipschitz triangular norms, and let C_tilde_a be the closure, under uniform convergence, of all convex combinations of elements of C_a. Does C_tilde_a coincide exactly with the class of all bivariate copulas that are both Schur-concave and commutative?

For C_tilde_a, the uniform-closure of convex combinations of associative bivariate copulas, determine its extremal points in the Krein-Milman sense. In addition, decide whether every extremal point of C_tilde_a is also an extremal point of the class of all bivariate copulas.

Describe the class C* of all binary operations obtained by transforming a bivariate copula C with a strictly increasing bijection phi:[0,1] -> [0,1] via C_phi(x,y)=phi^{-1}(C(phi(x),phi(y))). The description should account for the fact that such transforms need not be copulas and that the resulting class is strictly contained in the class of continuous semicopulas.

For n-ary quasi-copulas Q on [0,1]^n, characterize the intermediate class F consisting of those Q whose Q-volume is nonnegative on every n-dimensional Cartesian interval I for which at least one vertex of I lies on the boundary of the unit hypercube [0,1]^n. Also characterize natural distinguished subclasses of F.

For n-ary semicopulas S on [0,1]^n, characterize the class G consisting of those S whose S-volume is nonnegative for every n-dimensional Cartesian interval whose top vertex is the top vertex of the unit hypercube [0,1]^n. Also characterize natural distinguished subclasses of G.

Characterize all commutative and associative binary operations O:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] with neutral element 1 for which the induced map beta_O on finite subsets of [0,1], defined by beta_O({x1,...,xn})=O(x1,O(x2,...,O(x_{n-1},xn))), is a witness map. In this setting, being a witness map means that beta_O(empty set)=1, beta_O({x})=x, and for every finite A subset [0,1] and every X subset A, the alternating sum over all Z with X subset Z subset A of (-1)^{|X|+|Z|} beta_O(Z) is nonnegative.

Describe all triangular norms T, without assuming left-continuity, that satisfy T(x, 1 - T(1 - x, x)) = x for every x in [0,1]. This equation arises from requiring standard alpha-cuts of fuzzy sets to coincide with T-based alpha-cuts of the corresponding intuitionistic fuzzy sets.

Given two different triangular norms T1 and T2 with T1 <= T2 pointwise, define their opposite diagonal splice [T1,T2] by [T1,T2](x,y)=T2(x,y) when x+y-1>0 and [T1,T2](x,y)=T1(x,y) otherwise. Characterize, as completely as possible, all such pairs (T1,T2) for which the opposite diagonal splice is again a triangular norm.

Characterize all triples (S1,S2,T), where S1 and S2 are triangular conorms and T is a triangular norm, such that for every x,y in [0,1] the equality S1(x,y)=S2(T(x,y), T(1-x,y), T(x,1-y)) holds, with S2 applied iteratively according to its associativity. This is a fuzzy-set analogue of decomposing A union B into (A intersection B), (B minus A), and (A minus B).

For a fixed triangular norm T0 and triangular conorm S0, characterize all pairs (T,S), where T is a triangular norm and S is a triangular conorm, satisfying T(x,y)+S(x,y)=T0(x,y)+S0(x,y) for every x,y in [0,1]. This generalizes the Frank functional equation, which is obtained when T0 is one of the Lukasiewicz, product, or minimum triangular norms and S0 is its dual.

Provide an alternative characterization of all quasi-triangular norms. Here a track is a set {(f(t),g(t)): t in [0,1]} where f and g are nondecreasing continuous surjections from [0,1] to [0,1], and a binary operation U on [0,1] is a quasi-triangular norm if for every track B there exists a triangular norm T_B that agrees with U on B.

In a sharply dominating Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebra, every nonzero element x has a unique basic decomposition x = w_x plus the orthogonal sum of kappa-indexed atom multiples k_kappa a_kappa, where w_x is sharp, the a_kappa are atoms, and each k_kappa is a positive integer not equal to the order of a_kappa. Does every sharply dominating homogeneous Archimedean atomic effect algebra admit an analogous decomposition property of its elements by atoms of the algebra?

Let E be a sharply dominating homogeneous Archimedean atomic effect algebra, and let S(E) be the set of sharp elements of E. If S(E) admits an order-continuous state, does it follow that E itself admits a state?

For an Archimedean atomic effect algebra E with atomic center C(E), find conditions equivalent to the effect-algebraic sum of all atoms of C(E), computed in E, being equal to 1. Also find conditions equivalent to the equality between the sum of an arbitrary subset D of C(E) computed in E and the corresponding sum computed in C(E), whenever at least one of these sums exists.
